content.user_title: Improve SwiftUI Code with Expert Guidance
content.value_statement: SwiftUI projects can accumulate state, layout, accessibility, and performance problems. This skill provides focused review guidance and optional Instruments trace analysis to identify practical improvements.
actual_capabilities: Reviews SwiftUI state ownership, bindings, observable models, and view identity.
Guides list, layout, navigation, animation, accessibility, localization, and preview improvements.
Identifies modern API replacements and version-gating requirements from bundled references.
Explains performance patterns that reduce unnecessary view updates and expensive body work.
Records or analyzes Xcode Instruments traces when the user explicitly requests profiling.
limitations: Requires project code or trace data to make project-specific recommendations.
Does not run a profiling session without a user-selected target and recording scope.
Trace workflows require Xcode Instruments and xctrace on a supported Apple development environment.
Provides guidance and analysis; it does not replace device testing or Apple platform documentation.

use_cases.title: Review a feature screen
use_cases.description: Find state, identity, accessibility, and API issues before a SwiftUI feature is merged.

use_cases.title: Modernize an application
use_cases.description: Plan focused migrations from soft-deprecated SwiftUI APIs with appropriate availability fallbacks.

use_cases.title: Investigate performance
use_cases.description: Interpret an Instruments trace to prioritize hangs, hitches, CPU hotspots, and excessive SwiftUI updates.

prompt_templates.title: Review a SwiftUI view
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SwiftUI view for state ownership, accessibility, and view identity. Explain the highest-priority fixes first.

prompt_templates.title: Improve list performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SwiftUI list for stable identity, row structure, filtering, and unnecessary updates. Suggest targeted changes only.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an API migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Find soft-deprecated SwiftUI APIs in this file. Propose modern replacements with availability gates and fallbacks.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze an Instruments trace
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Instruments trace for the largest SwiftUI performance problems. Prioritize findings with trace evidence and recommend source areas to inspect.

output_examples.input: Review a SwiftUI settings screen with editable profile data.
output: Priority: keep view-owned draft data private in state.
Priority: use bindings only for fields that modify parent-owned data.
Accessibility: add labels to icon-only controls.

output_examples.input: Analyze a trace that shows repeated updates during scrolling.
output: Finding: repeated view updates overlap the scrolling interval.
Next step: inspect the source of broad environment writes.
Recommendation: move derived filtering outside the view body.

best_practices: Provide the relevant SwiftUI files and the deployment targets before requesting changes.
Ask for a review before requesting broad refactoring of a production feature.
Use a narrowly scoped Instruments recording target and confirm the data that may be captured.
anti_patterns: Do not request system-wide recording unless it is necessary and the data scope is approved.
Do not apply API migrations without testing availability gates on supported platform versions.
Do not treat trace recommendations as proof without inspecting the related source and reproducing the issue.

faq.question: What platforms does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers SwiftUI work for iOS and macOS, including platform-specific references where available.

faq.question: Can it write SwiftUI code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can propose or edit SwiftUI code when the user asks for implementation changes.

faq.question: Can it review existing code?
faq.answer: Yes. It reviews state, identity, composition, performance, accessibility, and API availability.

faq.question: Does it require Instruments?
faq.answer: No. Instruments is only needed for the optional trace recording and analysis workflows.

faq.question: How does trace recording protect privacy?
faq.answer: The recorder requires an explicit system-wide confirmation and redacts displayed launch environment values.

faq.question: Can it replace device testing?
faq.answer: No. Recommendations require validation through builds, tests, and testing on supported devices.
